findings.title: Hidden origins and witnessed results within one knowing
findings.claim: The unseen and witnessed can be read as the full span of divine knowing across transformations: concealed origins and outcomes that enter observation remain within one field of knowledge.
findings.mechanism: The focus names the Knower over both domains. The formation-to-sense sequence in 32:7–9, hidden recompense in 32:17, traces of destroyed generations in 32:26, and visible growth in 32:27 give distinct cases of what is concealed or witnessed. The human testimony in 12:81 is explicitly bounded by what its speakers knew and what they could not guard.
findings.reader_payoff: The pair becomes dynamic: what is hidden from ordinary observers and what later becomes perceptible are both within the named knowledge.
findings.containment: This does not make each scene one process or give humans access to all hidden things. The 32:7–9 examples come through a legacy reader account; the wider anchors have exact Arabic but their target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The published focus anchors are trusted; the contextual sequence and HFT mappings are legacy-unbound, with exact Arabic supplied for the cited later anchors and no target-side morphology.

findings.title: Surviving dwellings as signs of an absent history
findings.claim: The visible scene of people walking through the dwellings of destroyed generations can function as witness to an absent past: the remains are present, while their former inhabitants are not.
findings.mechanism: The focus's Knower, unseen domain, and witnessed domain meet 32:26's destroyed generations, present walkers, surviving homes, and explicit signs. The relation turns dwelling remains into evidence from which the absent history can be inferred.
findings.reader_payoff: A witnessed place can point toward people and events that are no longer directly visible.
findings.containment: The source leaves open that the dwellings function only as warning examples rather than a general theory of witness. The HFT word roles are attributed; target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The HFT source supplies exact Arabic and coordinates for all context roles; branch identities and their relation to the focus remain attributed.

findings.title: Water, hidden growth, and visible crop
findings.claim: The focus attributes can be read through an ecological sequence: force delivers water to barren land, concealed roots and growth emerge, and visible crop becomes something people are asked to see.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace maps hidden roots to the unseen, a condition-sign to the witnessed domain, resistant ground to might, and womb-like nurture to mercy. The context sequence then supplies driven water, irrigation, barren land, emergence, crop, and sight.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired attributes become an action grammar in which force and nurture bring hidden life into visible result.
findings.containment: The root mappings and the hard-ground and womb images are attributed, not target-side lexical analysis. The sequence may be one analogy for resurrection rather than a general reading of the attributes.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches have supplied registry glosses and facets; context words have exact Arabic anchors and matching coordinates, but their HFT root roles are attributed.

findings.title: The unseen and witnessed across an opening threshold
findings.claim: The hidden and witnessed can be read as successive states around an irreversible opening: a still-hidden future becomes judgment in the open, and the interval before it remains a possible space of response.
findings.mechanism: The focus pair meets the question about when the opening arrives in 32:28, the loss of benefit and delay on its day in 32:29, and reciprocal waiting in 32:30. Might marks the threshold's inaccessibility; mercy can make the remaining interval feel like opportunity.
findings.reader_payoff: The pair gains a temporal dimension: before the opening there is waiting, after it the event is witnessed and delay closes.
findings.containment: The merciful quality of the waiting interval is an attributed possibility; the source also says the waiting may be procedural. The focus itself does not state a timetable.

epistemic.reason: The HFT word coordinates match the supplied 32:28–30 Arabic; branch roles remain legacy-attributed and target morphology is absent.

findings.title: Spending imagined as a hidden conduit
findings.claim: Exploratorily, spending can be pictured as entering a hidden conduit: the visible act passes into an unseen reserve, where the focus's womb-like image supplies protected transformation before recompense returns.
findings.mechanism: The ordinary spending word provides visible outflow; the HFT trace adds unresolved tunnel and hidden-exit branches at the same surface, then connects concealment and recompense in 32:17 back to the focus's unseen and mercy carriers.
findings.reader_payoff: A visible act can be imagined as entering a route whose outcome is not yet visible to the giver.
findings.containment: The tunnel and hidden-exit images are intentionally branch-distant and are not lexical equations for the spending verb. The source's simpler alternative—visible deed followed by unknown reward—remains live; all unresolved HFT roles stay attributed.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic coordinates match the named surfaces, but the trace uses intentionally distant branch images and the reader identity is legacy-unbound.

findings.title: Might as enablement of patient guides
findings.claim: One attributed effect of the focus's might is enabling patient people to become guides; the text presents their appointment, leadership, and direction as an outcome of divine making.
findings.mechanism: The focus's strengthening branch meets the appointment of leaders from within a community, their guidance, and the patience preceding it. This yields an effect of might distributed through human agents.
findings.reader_payoff: Might can be perceived through what it enables, while the human guides remain distinct from the divine attribute.
findings.containment: The source's kinship branch is excluded: being made leaders from among a group does not establish shared ancestry. No transfer of the attribute is claimed, and guidance is tied to the stated patience.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates and roots match 32:24's supplied Arabic; target morphology is absent and the interpersonal reading remains attributed.

findings.title: The paired attributes as a ground for reliance
findings.claim: The paired names can also be received as a ground for reliance: a wider verse directly commands trust in the Mighty, Merciful One.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the two attributes; 26:217 repeats them as the object of a command to rely, changing the pair from description into a concrete orientation for the reader.
findings.reader_payoff: The attributes can guide a response as well as name a quality.
findings.containment: The command belongs to 26:217, not to the wording of 32:6. The target Arabic is supplied, but its morphology is not part of this packet.

epistemic.reason: The exact target wording and connection note supply a direct parallel, but no trust label or target morphology is attached to the connection record.

friction_notes: focus_word_alignment resolves all seven focus word-analysis units. The wider HFT anchors have exact Arabic, but target morphology and independent root analyses are absent, so their branch roles remain attributed.

The formation-to-life examples in 32:7–9 come through legacy reader text; the death, judgment, history, ecological, and temporal contexts have exact Arabic anchors but still retain source-attributed branch mappings.
